title: Review the defaults-loop design against records, code and Jev gateway
summary: Write a review of docs/design/defaults-loop.md at docs/design/reviews/defaults-loop-review-1.md. It checks the design's evidence against the records it cites, its claims against the code, and its assumptions about Jev against the gateway behavior the user probed. It ends with a verdict of accept, accept with changes, or reject, and changes nothing else.

defaults_applied.how: Every review finding cites a record, a file path, or the user's probe, and any number is labeled measured or estimated.
The review is written so an outside reader can follow it without the conversation.
One new file, and nothing else changes.
Findings name the underlying design flaw, not just the one instance.
The review includes no secrets or personal data, such as the user's email.

assumptions: The design doc and the records it cites exist as the user describes; I did not read them in this pass.
The probe figures come from the user and cannot be reproduced here. The review labels them user-reported.
The cost in the request is garbled ('/bin/bash.000017'). The review quotes it as the user wrote it, flagged as unreadable, and does not guess a value.
Existing reviews in docs/design/reviews/ set the format.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/reviews/defaults-loop-review-1.md exists and follows the layout of existing reviews in docs/design/reviews/.
The review checks the design's evidence against the records it cites, and notes any cited record that is absent or does not support the claim.
The review checks the design's claims against the code, citing file paths for each claim it confirms or refutes.

The review checks the design against the Jev gateway facts: /v1/chat/completions refuses Jev; the call is POST /v1/evaluate with model, state and questions (boolean or choice, with instructions and criteria); the answer has choice, per-option probabilities and confidence; fallback runs through providerOptions.gateway.models with when.confidenceBelow.

The review reports the probe result (changelog 0.90, none 0.06, designed 0.04, confidence 0.87, 409 input and 59 output tokens) as the user's measurement, and says what it does and does not show, since it is one probe.
The review ends with a verdict line: accept, accept with changes listed (the changes enumerated), or reject.
No file other than the review is changed, and the design doc is not edited.

out_of_scope: Editing docs/design/defaults-loop.md or applying the review's changes.
Changing code, tests, configuration or CHANGELOG.md.
Calling the gateway or Jev; the probe results come from the user.
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference, because the review must read the design, its cited records and the code before writing.
